**2h**

This session I designed the Bible of the lock (the part that the core goes into) and the Bible cover. I had some issues designing the Bible cover because I wasn't exactly sour how I wanted it to interact with the Bible, but I'm pretty happy with the solution I ended up on because it's pretty simple and should be reliable and easy to assemble. ### 2026-10-18: This afternoon I had a VERY long session. I needed to get this project done before the deadline tonight, and I somehow finished it.

**7h**

This afternoon I had a VERY long session. I needed to get this project done before the deadline tonight, and I somehow finished it. 

I started out by doing some more 3d modeling. I'm still not great at it, but I can tell that I'm getting better. I modified the plug to hold a C-clip, and then modeled the C-clip itself. After this I modeled the driver pin and 7 different lengths of Key pin for the lock. After joining all of these together in an assembly, I finished the model!

With this project, I wanted to be able to generate any key that I wanted, so with a little help from ai, I was able to create a script that can generate a key from a given key code, so that why anyone who prints the lock can have their own unique key. This was a LOT more complicated than I though, and took over half of this session to finish. I ended up needing 16 variations of the script to get it right, but I'm pretty satisfied with the final product!

After this, I added some stuff to the Github and wrote the README as well as making the Bill of Materials.

## Build

### 2026-11-26: This session I spent a while refining the key generating python script for this project. The previous one worked, but I wanted to make it so that the script would also automatically compile all of the

**4h**

This session I spent a while refining the key generating python script for this project. The previous one worked, but I wanted to make it so that the script would also automatically compile all of the correct STLs into one STL so that the user doesn't have to pick out all of pin files individually and keep track of 50 different files at the same time. This was relatively easy compared to what I had done with the key generation and it made it much easier now that I know how to use the python mesh editing libraries. 

After finished this, I still didn't like the way it turned out because the script still had to be in a folder with all of the STLs for it to work. I wanted it to be able to work entirely on its own so the user doesn't need to download 15 different STLs. The way I did this was by encoding all of the STLs with Base64 and including this encrypted text into the python script. This way, it doesn't rely on any external files for it to work, and now the user only needs one file downloaded in order to make a lock with a custom keycode. 

I also uploaded this new improvement to the GitHub and uploaded the README

### 2026-11-27: This session I finally assembled my lock! I ended up making two so that I could demonstrate how differnet key work in different locks.

**3.5h**

This session I finally assembled my lock! I ended up making two so that I could demonstrate how differnet key work in different locks. 

Post processing took a LOT longer than I thought. Turns out when you're printing out a mechanism with a lot of moving parts and tight tolerance an Ender 3 isn't the best tool of choice. I ended up having to sand and debur every single part, include all 20 pins for the two locks, and this was NOT easy with how small the pins are. However, I ended up getting everything sorted, assembled it all, and now I have two working locks!
